page: Amazon Web Services m8a.12xlarge is an eighth-generation general-purpose virtual machine based on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by the AMD EPYC 9R45 processor using the x86_64 architecture, providing 48 dedicated physical cores operating at up to 4.5 GHz with a single thread per core execution model. The instance configuration includes 192.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory operating at 6 GHz, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The processor supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16 extensions, alongside dedicated hardware acceleration for cryptographic workloads.

Benchmark evaluations confirm top-tier compute and memory subsystem performance. Stress-ng yields 3,778.18 in single-core and 178,949.7 in multi-core metrics, positioning the compute capacity within the top 10% of cloud profiles. Geekbench evaluations reflect similarly elevated results, recording a multi-core score of 29,981.0 and a software compilation score of 78,402.0. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth reaches 290.37 GB/sec, while write bandwidth achieves 178.08 GB/sec. The instance delivers high throughput in network and memory-bound operations, exceeding 154 million operations per second on Redis SET benchmarks and reaching 91.57 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

The hardware configuration features trade-offs concerning storage and specialization. The instance does not include bundled local NVMe storage, requiring network-attached storage architectures for persistent data needs. Dedicated hardware acceleration is absent due to a zero GPU allocation. Nonetheless, the CPU architecture provides competent quantized model execution, reaching 55.44 tokens per second during text generation on 7B parameter models. Networking is provisioned with a baseline bandwidth of 22 Gbps.

The instance delivers high operational resource density and cost efficiency for general-purpose infrastructure through its dedicated physical core layout and fast DDR5 memory. Suitable workloads include large-scale enterprise microservices, intermediate-scale relational and in-memory databases, Clang-based software build clusters, multi-threaded batch data processing pipelines, and high-throughput static web serving fleets.
description: Amazon Web Services m8a.12xlarge is an eighth-generation general-purpose instance powered by 48 dedicated AMD EPYC 9R45 cores on the x86_64 architecture, operating at up to 4.5 GHz without multithreading overhead. It integrates 192.0 GB of high-frequency 6 GHz DDR5 memory, yielding a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, the platform provides 22 Gbps baseline networking capacity. It incorporates no integrated local storage or discrete GPU accelerators, depending entirely on remote block storage solutions. Benchmark measurements demonstrate top-tier execution across multi-core computing, software compilation, and in-memory throughput, with Redis operations exceeding 154 million SET requests per second. Given its physical core density and fast DDR5 subsystem, this instance is suitable for intensive enterprise application servers, memory-centric key-value databases, continuous integration build farms, and multi-threaded analytical processing.
